column1: # SHA-256 manifest of the FROZEN AMRFinderPlus dated database 2026-05-15.1.
# A conda lockfile pins software packages.  This database is not in the package:
# AMRFinderPlus downloads it separately, and `amrfinder -u` only ever fetches the
# LATEST database.  There is no command anywhere that asks NCBI for a specific
# dated version.  So the version string `amrfinder --database_version` prints is a
# LABEL -- anyone can create a directory and call it 2026-05-15.1 -- while the
# digests below are the EVIDENCE.  This file is what lets any machine, offline,
# answer "is this the same database that produced the recorded calls?".
# WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO
# It proves SAMENESS, not availability.  It cannot make NCBI serve 2026-05-15.1
# again.  If the local archive is lost and NCBI has moved on, the pinned database
# is UNRECOVERABLE: this manifest will then only be able to tell a future
# maintainer that whatever they have is not it.  Keeping a copy of the 239.4 MB
# directory somewhere durable is therefore part of the pin, not an optional extra.
# HOW THE ROLL-UP DIGEST IS COMPUTED (deterministic, and reproducible with
#   1. list every REGULAR file in the dated directory, as a path relative to that
#      directory (the directory is flat: 162 files, no sub-directories, no
#      symlinks, so every path is a bare file name);
#   2. sort those paths ascending by raw bytes (LC_ALL=C, not a locale collation);
#   3. for each one, emit the line `<sha256><two spaces><path>` followed by \n --
#   4. sha256 the concatenation of those lines.
# Sizes are recorded for people reading this file, not for the check: they are NOT
# part of the roll-up, which is over the sorted (name, hash) pairs only.  Folding
# them in later would move the roll-up without any file having changed.
#   find . -type f -printf '%P\n' | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs -d '\n' sha256sum
#   find . -type f -printf '%P\n' | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs -d '\n' sha256sum | sha256sum
# The first command prints the per-file lines (same digests as column 3 below);
# the second prints rollup_sha256.  Both need GNU find/xargs, which is what the
# Inside the pinned prefix, at share/amrfinderplus/data/2026-05-15.1, with a RELATIVE
# `latest` symlink beside it.  Inside, because a database found through an ambient
# CONDA_PREFIX belongs to some other install and would stamp the wrong version into
# the ledger.  The prefix itself is machine-local working state and is never
# committed -- 239.4 MB does not belong in a repository, but 162 lines do.
# HEADER FIELDS (read by bin/curation-triage/setup_envs.sh and by
#   database_version  what `amrfinder --database_version` prints for this database
#   files             number of regular files digested below
#   rollup_sha256     the digest defined above; also recorded in
#   frozen_on         the day this manifest was taken from the installed database
#   path         file name, relative to the dated database directory
